studies.Title: Soy product and isoflavone consumption in relation to prostate cancer in Japanese men.
studies.Reference: Soy product and isoflavone consumption in relation to prostate cancer in Japanese men.
Authors: Japan Public Health Center-Based Prospective Study Group
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Here, we conducted a population-based prospective study in 43,509 Japanese men ages 45 to 74 years who generally have a high intake of isoflavones and low incidence of prostate cancer. Participants responded to a validated questionnaire, which included 147 food items.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: During follow-up from 1995 through 2004, 307 men were newly diagnosed with prostate cancer, of which 74 cases were advanced, 220 cases were organ localized, and 13 cases were of an undetermined stage.
extraction_supporting_text.design: Here, we conducted a population-based prospective study
extraction_supporting_text.continent: The incidence of prostate cancer is much lower in Asian than Western populations.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Participants responded to a validated questionnaire, which included 147 food items.

studies.display_only_reason: Eligible study; JBI Fair is below the default pooling threshold.
studies.direction_imputation_reason: Comparison direction was not explicit; the protocol assumes high versus low exposure.
